item.title: “中国通过艰难谈判争取到了全球最多配额”
item.description:
欧盟委员会（简称“欧委会”）24日发布混动汽车全球保障措施初步裁定，并拟于12月1日起采取临时保障措施。届时，中国、英国、土耳其、日本、韩国等9个主要贸易伙伴，在向欧盟出口混合动力汽车时将受到配额限制。临时措施为期200天，中国配额为19.2万辆，折合成年度配额为35万辆，高于其他所有进口来源地。


值得关注的是，在10月份中欧双方就混动汽车贸易进行磋商之前，欧方高度关注中国混动汽车对欧出口快速增长势头，曾计划专门针对中国混合动力汽车进行限制。而中方在欧盟正式发起保障措施调查前，坚持尊重事实、非歧视、合规三原则，通过立案前磋商，与欧方就混动汽车贸易达成了合法合规、务实平衡的安排，有力维护了中国企业的实际利益，避免了中欧贸易摩擦局面升级。接受《环球时报》记者采访的专家表示，中国通过艰难谈判争取到了全球最多的对欧混动汽车出口份额，维护了中国汽车业的利益。中国有能力、有智慧解决中欧贸易分歧。


《环球时报》记者注意到，临时措施采取数量配额形式，以2025年欧盟实际进口量为基准，为中国、英国、土耳其、日本、韩国等9个主要贸易伙伴设定了进口配额。根据世贸组织规则，临时措施期限为200天。


在200天中，中国配额为19.2万辆，日本、土耳其、英国、韩国、墨西哥、摩洛哥、塞尔维亚、美国的配额分别为17.1、12.6、10.5、6.8、3.4、2.4、1.9、1.8万辆。所有其他国家配额为822辆。


欧委会在24日的新闻稿中称，采取这些限制措施，是为了保护欧盟产业免受近期此类车辆进口激增的冲击。此前的一项调查显示，自2023年以来欧盟混合动力车进口量大幅增长。


中国机电商会法律服务部主任陈惠清24日在接受《环球时报》记者采访时表示，磋商过程十分艰苦，最终成果得来不易，对中方总体有利。一是，避免了欧盟对中国单独设限。配额同等适用于包括欧自贸伙伴在内的所有进口来源地。二是，欧方承诺，将以全流程符合世贸组织规则的方式开展调查和采取措施。三是，中国获得的配额数量最多，并且是在2025年实际贸易数据基础上作出的向上安排，保障了中国企业的实际出口利益。


陈惠清表示，欧方起初企图按照保障措施通常做法，用2022-2024年三年进口均值计算配额，仅给中方7万辆年度配额，而日本配额将达25.7万辆。最终磋商结果中方争取到35万辆年度配额，高于2025年欧盟自华进口30.2万辆数量，超过了日本等欧其他贸易伙伴。“与欧其他贸易伙伴相比，中国在欧盟混动汽车保障措施调查中抢占先机、占据主导。”陈惠清说。


《环球时报》记者注意到，近期，在世贸组织保障措施例会和货物贸易理事会等场合，日本、英国、韩国、土耳其等纷纷就欧盟混动汽车保障措施案表达关注，尤其不满欧方“立案前与特定贸易伙伴单独磋商”“调查预设结论”。


陈惠清说，目前商会正在和企业商讨行业自律协议，让企业能够有序、有规划地对欧盟出口，充分利用好配额。“这会促进中企出口更高端、利润更高的车型，实现更高质量的发展。”


中国汽车工业协会产业研究部研究专员黄心茹对《环球时报》记者分析说，35万辆配额，较前期出口基数有所提升，为我国混动汽车对欧出口稳定了基本盘，为企业经营提供了可预期的贸易环境。但该配额水平低于行业扩张预期，将对出口放量节奏形成约束，迫使行业从规模优先转向高质量出海，加快推进欧洲本地化生产与产业链布局。协会将引导企业科学规划出口节奏，规避低价和无序竞争。


对外经济贸易大学国家安全与治理研究院研究员梁怀新告诉《环球时报》记者，35万的配额，在一定程度上保证了中国新能源汽车的对欧出口整体规模，避免出现对欧新能源汽车出口锐减的局面，为中欧新能源汽车贸易稳定发展留出了空间。


这位学者进一步说，此次磋商成果进一步体现了对话合作、尊重世贸组织规则在解决贸易争端中的重要意义。一方面，中国一直秉持开放态度，积极推动同欧盟等主体进行新能源汽车贸易谈判，通过对话磋商解决贸易分歧，临时措施在一些条款上的具体设计，体现了中方的努力，和欧盟方面的“听劝”。如果欧盟方面能够继续与中国相向而行，没有什么贸易摩擦是不能通过对话和合作化解的。同时，中欧对话中世贸组织规则的嵌入，体现了世贸规则在解决当前新能源汽车贸易摩擦中的适用性，欧盟方面需要认识到必须在世贸规则下才能与各方共同达成最优的贸易解决方案。


中欧双方已经就混动汽车、电动汽车贸易进行了30余轮密集磋商。“中国有能力、有智慧解决中欧贸易分歧。”陈惠清表示，汽车是中欧双方都非常关注的产业，这个问题处理好了，能够避免贸易摩擦升级。“实际上，我们从中拿到了实实在在的利益，也解决了欧方的一些合理关切。”


“就像现在比较火的一首歌的歌词一样，面对全球新能源汽车贸易浪潮，欧盟‘慌啥子嘛’，只要欧盟与中国等贸易伙伴‘慢慢来，找到大家共同的节奏’，心平气和地沟通对话，大家可以相向而行，共同找到各方都能接受的最优方案，保证各国新能源汽车企业与消费者的共同利益，推动全球新能源汽车贸易的进一步发展。”梁怀新说。


商务部新闻发言人24日表示，此前，中欧双方本着相互尊重、平等协商的原则，在中欧贸易投资磋商机制项下进行了立案前磋商，并就混动汽车贸易达成了合法合规、务实平衡的安排。希望欧方切实遵守双方共识，严格依照世贸组织规则，不折不扣落实非歧视原则，公平、公正开展相关调查。中方将密切关注欧方后续调查进展，保留在世贸组织框架下诉诸争端解决、要求贸易补偿等一切权利，坚决维护中国相关产业正当权益。



环球时报记者 陈子帅

item.title: 法国，“财政濒临窒息”
item.description:
法国总统马克龙日前表示，正考虑尝试将限制财政赤字的预算“黄金法则”写入宪法，以规避金融危机风险。法媒分析称，此举旨在安抚市场和债权人。然而，欧盟预算规则约束早已存在，多年未守财政纪律的法国能靠“黄金法则”扭转财政长期失衡的局面吗？


5日，巴黎一名示威者举着写有“不该由工人和养老金领取者偿还债务”的标语牌。（视觉中国）


债务体量“大到无法被拯救”？

法国《费加罗报》23日刊登了对马克龙的专访。他证实，确实在考虑尝试将预算“黄金法则”写入宪法，以规避金融危机风险，因为目前法国债务已达到3.6万亿欧元，且利率正在上升。

法媒分析，预算“黄金法则”可能借鉴了2011年萨科齐执政时期提出的一项宪法改革提案。该提案并未明确设定任何特定年度的赤字上限，而是制定了一个涵盖多年的框架，要求预算长期保持收支平衡。“黄金法则”的核心目的是向市场和债权人发出“法国将管住钱袋”的可信信号。

不过，预算“黄金法则”这一工具没有确切的定义。法国欧洲新闻台称，大体而言，它是一种预算规范。马克龙认为，实施这样的措施可以安抚市场，因为目前法国在公共财政管理方面堪称欧盟的“差等生”。英国《金融时报》称，法国财政赤字在欧盟处于较高水平，预计今年将占GDP的5.4%。据欧盟委员会预测，到2028年，法国财政赤字将占其GDP的近6%。多位经济学家更将当下的法国与债务危机前的希腊相提并论。法国经济学家图阿蒂分析称，2010年希腊债务约3500亿欧元，国际货币基金组织、欧盟与欧洲央行尚能合力“拯救”；而法国今天的债务体量，恐怕“大到无法被拯救”。

勒庞的支持

《费加罗报》提到，在法国总统大选即将来临的背景下，此举被视为马克龙“仍有改革意愿”。马克龙将于明年春季卸任。在其执政十年后，法国公共财政状况恶化，他因此遭到竞争对手的猛烈抨击。《金融时报》称，马克龙此举呼应了那些批评其财政政策的政治对手们的提议。

法国2027年总统选举国民联盟候选人勒庞支持这一措施。她上月在法国《观点报》撰文称，她支持通过把预算“黄金法则”写入宪法来削减公共支出，以迫使未来政府遵守赤字目标。勒庞称，“经过半个多世纪的财政赤字和十年的‘马克龙式挥霍’，法国深陷公共财政的灾难性泥潭，这正将我们的国家推向一场金融、经济和道德危机的边缘。法国必须重建外界对我们重新掌控公共财政能力的信任。”

《金融时报》称，勒庞领导的国民联盟一直试图将自身塑造为财政上负责任的政党。勒庞表示，国民联盟“已经要求”现任政府考虑就此事在议会两院进行投票。

不过，法国政坛也不乏反对“黄金法则”的声音。据法国《巴黎人报》报道，左翼“不屈法国”成员科克雷尔谴责这项改革，称其“将严格限制未来政府推行其他经济政策的能力”。他还说，这项提案无异于“将新自由主义噩梦写入宪法”。

“马克龙试图以新预算规则束缚继任者。”美国“政治新闻网”欧洲版23日的文章这样解读马克龙的举动。文章称，马克龙的反对者——甚至他的一些盟友——并不认同这种缓解市场担忧的逻辑。法国共和党主席布鲁诺·勒塔约在社交媒体上写道：“马克龙直到任内第十份预算案出现巨额赤字时才考虑此事，这充分说明，这位总统直到把金库掏空，才决定把金库锁起来。”

灵丹妙药还是政治博弈？

那么“黄金法则”是否是能够一举扭转法国财政长期失衡困局的灵丹妙药？事实上，“黄金法则”这样的机制早已有之。欧盟《稳定与增长公约》原则上要求成员国的财政赤字低于GDP的3%，法国显然并未遵守欧盟制定的财政纪律。

更深层的风险在于法国社会当下的脆弱。《环球时报》驻法国特约记者发现，里昂等大城市主街的店铺纷纷用钢板和木架护住橱窗，圣诞将至，消费气氛却远逊从前，街道上弥漫着不安。加拿大广播公司法语频道报道称，在距大选半年之际，法国正经历“艰难财政困局”，10月反对高生活成本示威演变为暴力冲突和劫掠，商户损失以数亿欧元计。在这样的氛围下，一项以“长期平衡”为名、实则指向削减公共开支的政策，极可能被民众读作新一轮紧缩的信号。

还有经济学家认为，如果“黄金法则”严格适用于全部支出，就会对投资构成重大阻碍。即使是以财政纪律严格著称的德国，最近也同意对“黄金法则”作出例外规定，并启动一项大规模经济刺激计划。

路透社称，“黄金法则”提案2011年曾获得法国议会两院通过，但要将其正式写入宪法，还需进一步获得批准，可以通过全民公投，也可以由议会两院组成的联席会议以3/5多数表决通过。不过，欧洲新闻台称，在未来几个月内将“黄金法则”写入宪法的可能性相当小，因为这需要在极其有限的时间内在国民议会和参议院进行两轮审议，而议会会期将于2027年2月底结束。

法国新闻广播电台称，所有渴望在未来执政的人都不愿接手一个财政濒临窒息的国家，这显然是一场政治博弈。




环球时报驻法国特约记者 谢祎君 环球时报特约记者 任重

审核 | 徐璐明

编辑 | 于泽淼

校对 | 姚佰可

item.title: 为什么黄仁勋不可撼动
item.description:
STEPHEN WITT
2026年11月25日

When Jensen Huang returned to the floor of his Silicon Valley headquarters on Monday, his employees greeted him with a standing ovation. The rank and file of Nvidia love Mr. Huang, who has made many of them wealthy. In the midst of this celebration, I imagine his top executives must have exchanged a few glances. They know all about Mr. Huang’s abusive treatment of staff members, his extramarital relationships and Nvidia’s funny business in Southeast Asia. But, in the end, I’m sure they clapped, too.

周一，黄仁勋回到英伟达位于硅谷的总部时，员工们起立鼓掌欢迎。英伟达的普通员工都很爱戴黄仁勋，他让许多人赚得盆满钵满。在这欢庆的场面中，我想公司的高管们一定交换了几下眼神。他们对黄仁勋粗暴对待员工的行为、他的婚外情以及英伟达在东南亚那些见不得光的生意都心知肚明。不过，我相信最后他们也鼓掌了。

In the 11 days he was gone, Nvidia lost almost 30 percent of its value. Upon his return, Nvidia’s stock price recovered, adding almost a trillion dollars to the company’s market capitalization. They’re saying Jensen Huang is too big to fire. I say he’s the trillion-dollar man.

在他离开的11天里，英伟达市值损失近30%。他回归后，英伟达股价回升，公司市值增加近1万亿美元。人们说，黄仁勋重要到不能解雇。要我说，他是个价值万亿美元的男人。

Mr. Huang still has a number of looming scandals. Nvidia is being investigated by Congress, the Justice Department, the Securities and Exchange Commission and its own corporate board. The U.S. intelligence community seems to have compromising intelligence on Mr. Huang; he’s reportedly had numerous affairs, including one with a married corporate executive at his company and another with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

黄仁勋仍有多桩丑闻悬而未决。英伟达正受到国会、司法部、证券交易委员会及其自身董事会的调查。美国情报界似乎掌握了足以让黄仁勋陷入被动的情报；据报道，他有多次婚外情，包括与公司一名已婚女高管，以及与一名疑似中国间谍的女子。

Reporters have produced detailed accounts of his scathing encounters with staff members, which include bodily threats and ritual humiliation. He is scheduled to have a closed-door interview with House committees next Tuesday and to testify before the Senate two days later. For another corporate executive, any one of these scandals would be a career-killer. For Mr. Huang, it’s Monday morning.

记者们详细披露了他如何刻薄地对待员工，其中包括人身威胁和仪式化的羞辱。他定于下周二接受众议院多个委员会的闭门问询，并于两天后赴参议院作证。换作其他企业高管，这些丑闻中的任何一桩都足以断送职业生涯。对黄仁勋而言，这不过是一个寻常的周一早晨。

Mr. Huang’s invincibility derives from his close relationship with President Trump. Mr. Huang started cultivating this connection in 2025, when he and his wife, Lori, visited Mar-a-Lago. There, over dinner, he told Mr. Trump the compelling story of his rise from Denny’s waitstaff to semiconductor chief executive. In the course of writing Mr. Huang’s biography, I heard him tell this story many times. I never got tired of it — although I did notice the details change a bit at different tellings. The dazzled Mr. Trump fell hard for Mr. Huang. He also fell for Lori, whom on Monday he called a “fantastic woman” and “very supportive.”

黄仁勋之所以不可撼动，源于他与特朗普总统的密切关系。2025年，黄仁勋和妻子洛丽到访马阿拉歌庄园，从那时起，他便开始经营这段关系。席间，他向特朗普讲述了自己如何从连锁餐厅Denny's的一名服务员成长为半导体企业首席执行官的动人故事。在为黄仁勋撰写传记的过程中，我多次听他讲过这个故事，始终百听不厌——尽管我确实注意到，每次讲述的细节略有不同。听得入迷的特朗普彻底被黄仁勋征服了。他也很喜欢洛丽，周一还称她是个“了不起的女人”，对丈夫“非常支持”。

By the beginning of this year, Mr. Trump and Mr. Huang were talking often on the phone. When Marco Rubio, the president’s secretary of state and national security adviser, shared intelligence details about Mr. Huang’s romantic relationship with Alice Huang and the belief that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, Mr. Trump pooh-poohed it. Instead, he offered Mr. Huang a ride with him on Air Force One to meet with China’s president, Xi Jinping. The intelligence findings were eventually published by The Times, causing a cascade of revelations about Mr. Huang’s misbehaviors. Twelve days ago, Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted Mr. Huang’s resignation. But in the interim, the A.I. economy cratered, and when Mr. Trump pushed for him to be reinstated, the board unanimously voted to take him back.

到今年年初，特朗普和黄仁勋经常通电话。当国务卿兼国家安全顾问鲁比奥向他汇报了关于黄仁勋与黄乐的私情以及认为她是中国情报机构线人的细节时，特朗普不以为然。他反而邀请黄仁勋乘坐“空军一号”，随他一起会见中国国家主席习近平。《纽约时报》最终披露了这些情报调查结果，引发了一系列关于黄仁勋不当行为的爆料。12天前，英伟达董事会一致接受黄仁勋辞职。但在此期间，人工智能经济遭遇重挫，在特朗普力促黄仁勋复职后，董事会又一致投票同意让他回来。

Mr. Trump had reason to act: Nvidia’s plummeting stock price posed a threat to the global economy. When Nvidia underperforms, it drags the entire market down with it. By contrast, when Nvidia succeeds, it feeds a sprawling portfolio of data centers and developers. Mr. Huang is Nvidia; and Nvidia is A.I.; and A.I. is the American economy. To an extraordinary extent, the success of our stock market relies on this single man.

特朗普采取行动并非没有理由：英伟达股价暴跌对全球经济构成了威胁。英伟达表现不佳时，整个股市都会受到拖累。相反，英伟达的成功会带动庞大的数据中心和开发商群体。黄仁勋就是英伟达，英伟达就是人工智能，而人工智能就是美国经济。我们的股市能否繁荣，在很大程度上竟取决于这一个人。

I understand the board’s reasoning. It’s not the morality police. Its job is to make Nvidia’s stock price go up, and no one does that better than Mr. Huang. Several board members are themselves Nvidia billionaires, and some have been with Mr. Huang since Day 1. Also, what were they going to do — tell the president no?

我理解董事会的考量。它不是道德警察，它的职责是推动英伟达股价上涨，而在这方面，没有人比黄仁勋做得更好。几名董事会成员本身就是凭借英伟达股票跻身亿万富翁行列的，其中一些人从公司创立之初就追随黄仁勋。再说，他们又能怎么办呢——对总统说不吗？

And, it must be admitted, Mr. Huang truly is an irreplaceable businessman. He does the work of an entire C-suite. He is a manager, a thinker, a worker. He is a ruthless operations specialist, a customer relations whisperer, a talent scout and a strategic visionary. He can forecast the existence of new markets years in advance, and he can predict what the competitive dynamics of those markets will be once they come into being. In reporting on the growing humanoid robotics industry, I found that practically every such robot uses an Nvidia microchip for its brain — because Mr. Huang had directed Nvidia to start building these brains years before the robots existed.

而且，不得不承认，黄仁勋的确是一位无可替代的商界人士。他一个人就能承担整个高管团队的工作。他是管理者、思考者，也是实干家。他是无情的运营专家、深谙客户关系之道的高手、善于发掘人才的伯乐，以及富有远见的战略家。他能提前数年预见新市场的出现，还能预测这些市场形成后的竞争格局。在报道蓬勃发展的人形机器人产业时，我发现，几乎每一台此类机器人的大脑都采用了英伟达的微芯片——因为早在这些机器人问世之前，黄仁勋就已指示英伟达着手打造这些大脑。

Mr. Huang has many other talents. He is an accomplished public speaker — even though he has stage fright. He’s funny and charming and loves to tell jokes. He is an excellent draftsman and can draw, from memory, an elegant exploded diagram of one of his G.P.U.s. He can also label every part and tell you what it does, how much it costs and which of his Taiwanese suppliers he would pick up the phone to yell at if it were late. At 63, he retains a ton of energy and is surprisingly athletic. If Nvidia’s board had not rehired him, he could certainly have built a business to compete against the company.

黄仁勋还有许多其他才能。他是一位出色的演说家——尽管他也会怯场。他风趣迷人，喜欢讲笑话。他的制图功底十分出色，能凭记忆画出一张精美的英伟达图形处理器分解图。他还能标出每个零部件，告诉你它的用途、成本，如果该部件未能按时交货，他会打电话痛骂哪一家台湾供应商。63岁的他依然精力充沛，运动能力出奇地好。如果英伟达董事会没有重新聘用他，他完全有能力创办一家与英伟达竞争的企业。

In intervening to get Mr. Huang reinstated, Mr. Trump also played to the Main Street shareholder. Nvidia is one of the most popular stocks among retail investors, and its fame extends to unlikely places: While shooting clay pigeons in rural North Carolina earlier this year, I mentioned to a fellow shooter that I’d written a book about Nvidia. He pulled up his Robinhood account on his phone and walked me through his Nvidia trading history; then he yelled “pull” and nailed two targets in half a second. Such shareholders, I find, often have only a vague idea of what Nvidia makes. What they do know is that the stock should go up.

特朗普出面促成黄仁勋复职，也是在迎合普通股民。英伟达是散户投资者最青睐的股票之一，其知名度甚至超乎想象：今年早些时候，在北卡罗来纳州乡间打飞碟靶时，我向一位射击同伴提到自己写过一本关于英伟达的书。他立即在手机上打开自己的Robinhood账户，给我逐一介绍他买卖英伟达股票的记录；随后，他喊了一声“放靶”，半秒内就击中了两个目标。我发现，这类股东往往对英伟达究竟生产什么只有一个模糊的概念。但有一点他们很清楚：这只股票应该上涨。

But if Mr. Trump’s reinstatement is good for average investors, it is terrible for the rule of law. Nvidia may have broken the law and must be thoroughly investigated. In 2022, the Biden administration announced restrictions on sales to China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips. Nvidia responded by joining with new partners in Southeast Asia. These so-called cloud partners received preferential treatment when Nvidia was allocating its most advanced microchips, which, given the supply-demand imbalance for Nvidia equipment in late 2023, was sort of like the partners being handed a license to print money. The partners, mostly based in Singapore, were supposed to install the Nvidia-powered hardware they received in data centers in Malaysia. Instead, investigators say, some skirted the export ban by reselling the equipment to China.

然而，如果说特朗普促成黄仁勋复职有利于普通投资者，此举对法治而言则糟糕透顶。英伟达可能触犯了法律，必须受到彻底调查。2022年，拜登政府宣布限制英伟达最先进的芯片销往中国。作为回应，英伟达开始与东南亚的新合作伙伴开展业务。这些所谓的云服务合作伙伴在英伟达分配最先进的微芯片时享有优先待遇。鉴于2023年底英伟达的产品供不应求，这几乎等于给这些合作伙伴发了一张印钞许可证。这些合作伙伴大多位于新加坡，原本应将它们获得的搭载英伟达芯片的硬件设备安装到马来西亚的数据中心。然而，调查人员称，其中一些合作伙伴将设备转售给中国，绕过了出口禁令。

One cloud partner, Alan Wei Zhaolun, had accumulated enough money to buy a $40 million house. In February 2025, Mr. Zhaolun was arrested by the Singapore Police Force and accused of diverting his Nvidia chip allotment for resale to China. Singapore charged him with money laundering and fraud, and he could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. He has pleaded not guilty. (Nvidia says it stopped doing business with Mr. Zhaolun before his arrest.)

其中一家云服务合作伙伴的经营者韦兆伦积累的财富足以让他买下一栋价值4000万美元的豪宅。2025年2月，他被新加坡警方逮捕，被指将获配的英伟达芯片转售给中国。新加坡方面以洗钱和欺诈罪名对他提起指控，如果罪名成立，他可能面临最高20年的监禁。他表示不认罪。（英伟达表示在他被捕前已停止与他的业务往来。）

Alice Huang’s company was also a Nvidia cloud partner — and she was Jensen’s romantic partner, too. In June 2025, the Singapore Police questioned her and seized her passport. They returned it in February 2026 and later cited a lack of cooperation from the U.S. Department of Justice. Ms. Huang was banned from Singapore and now is reported to be in China. The U.S. intelligence community assessed her to be a Chinese intelligence asset whose company was suspected of diverting chips to China. (China denies this.)

黄乐的公司也是英伟达的云服务合作伙伴，而她本人是黄仁勋的情人。2025年6月，新加坡警方对她进行了问询，并扣押了她的护照。警方于2026年2月归还了她的护照，后来表示美国司法部不予配合。她已被禁止入境新加坡，据报道目前身在中国。美国情报界认定她是中国情报机构的线人，她的公司则涉嫌将芯片转运至中国。（中国否认这一点。）

I would like to know why Nvidia designated these two as preferred customers. I would like to know what suspicions Nvidia had about these and other Singapore-based businesses and what they did to respond. I would like to know why Nvidia changed its accounting procedures after sales in Singapore grew to 22 percent of its revenue. But I fear I may never get the complete answer.

我想知道为什么英伟达将这两个人指定为优先客户。我想知道英伟达对这些及其他新加坡企业存有哪些疑虑，又采取了什么应对措施。我还想知道，在新加坡的销售额增至公司营收的22%之后，英伟达为何改变了会计核算方式。但我担心，我可能永远得不到完整答案。

The U.S. Commerce Department, which was originally investigating alongside the Singapore Police Force, was transferred off the case after Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, directly emailed investigators and name-checked their boss. The Justice Department took over — and this, Singapore authorities say, was when their investigation into Alice Huang stalled. President Trump, with his endorsement of Mr. Huang, has signaled to Nvidia’s board that the F.B.I. will not find anything too damaging. I wonder how hard it’s really looking.

美国商务部原本与新加坡警方共同展开调查，但在英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特直接给调查人员发送电子邮件，并特意提及他们的上司后，商务部被调离了此案的调查工作。司法部接手了调查——新加坡当局称，正是在这时，他们对黄乐的调查陷入停滞。特朗普对黄仁勋的支持向英伟达董事会释放出一个信号：联邦调查局不会查出任何对他过于不利的东西。我不禁怀疑，调查到底有多认真。

Mr. Huang’s reinstatement also sends a terrible signal regarding the fair treatment of women in the workplace. Mr. Huang had affairs with at least two subordinates: Kimberly Powell, a married health care executive at his company, and another woman, identified by Reuters, who remains anonymous. On Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported that Mr. Huang admitted to more affairs.

黄仁勋的复职也在职场女性能否受到公平对待的问题上释放了一个极其恶劣的信号。黄仁勋至少与两名下属有过婚外情：一名是已婚的医疗保健业务高管金伯莉·鲍威尔，另一名是路透社查明身份但未公开姓名的女性。周一，《华尔街日报》报道称，黄仁勋承认还有其他婚外情。

He will very likely face few repercussions for actions that would get anyone else in America fired. In fact, his romantic misadventures are being celebrated — on Monday, Mr. Trump posted a meme that riffed on the famous “Fight!” moment from his own assassination attempt, showing Mr. Huang with a bloody face and waving a red bra. The joke signals a return to “Mad Men” standards of behavior. The broader cultural implications for women are depressing to contemplate.

这些行为若发生在美国其他任何人身上都足以导致其被解雇，而他很可能几乎不用承担任何后果。事实上，他那些荒唐的情事甚至成了人们津津乐道的事情——周一，特朗普发布了一张网络恶搞图片，以自己遭遇暗杀未遂时那个著名的高喊“战斗！”的瞬间为蓝本，画面中黄仁勋满脸是血，挥舞着一件红色胸罩。这个玩笑表明，人们的行为准则正在倒退回《广告狂人》(Mad Men)所描绘的时代。这对女性来说意味着怎样一种更广泛的社会文化影响，想想就令人沮丧。

In an early draft of “The Thinking Machine,” my biography of Mr. Huang, I opined that he was one of the great men of history. I took that phrase out but I wish I’d left it in. Mr. Huang is as great as he is terrible.

在黄仁勋传记《思考机器》（The Thinking Machine，中译《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》）的早期草稿中，我曾写道，他是历史伟人之一。后来我删掉了这句话，但现在我希望自己当初没有这样做。黄仁勋有多伟大，就有多可怕。

He’s a titan of industry who reinvented the computer from the transistor up. He also betrayed his wife, his employees, his company and possibly his country. He’s a warm and charismatic jokester with a humble demeanor. He’s also a narcissist, an egomaniac and a manipulator — and when he gets in one of his moods, he behaves like a petty, insecure tyrant.

他是一位产业巨擘，从晶体管这一最基础的层面彻底重塑了计算机。但他也背叛了妻子、员工、公司，甚至可能背叛了自己的国家。他热情而富有魅力，爱开玩笑，举止谦和。但他同时也是一个自恋、自大、善于操纵他人的人——一旦脾气发作，他的表现就像一个心胸狭窄、缺乏安全感的暴君。

He’s a complicated figure, no question, and once the Democrats take office in January, they will go after him hard. But if I were on the board of Nvidia, and I were asking myself what to do, there’s also no question whom I’d choose.

毫无疑问，他是一个复杂的人物。等到明年1月民主党人掌权，他们必将对他穷追猛打。但如果我是英伟达董事会的一员，面对该如何抉择的问题，我会选择谁同样毫无疑问。

Welcome back, Mr. Huang. We hardly missed you.

欢迎回来，黄先生。我们还没来得及想念你呢。

Stephen Witt是黄仁勋传记《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》(The Thinking Machine)的作者。

翻译：纽约时报中文网

item.title: 为什么黄仁勋不可撼动
item.description:
STEPHEN WITT
2026年11月25日

周一，黄仁勋回到英伟达位于硅谷的总部时，员工们起立鼓掌欢迎。英伟达的普通员工都很爱戴黄仁勋，他让许多人赚得盆满钵满。在这欢庆的场面中，我想公司的高管们一定交换了几下眼神。他们对黄仁勋粗暴对待员工的行为、他的婚外情以及英伟达在东南亚那些见不得光的生意都心知肚明。不过，我相信最后他们也鼓掌了。

在他离开的11天里，英伟达市值损失近30%。他回归后，英伟达股价回升，公司市值增加近1万亿美元。人们说，黄仁勋重要到不能解雇。要我说，他是个价值万亿美元的男人。

黄仁勋仍有多桩丑闻悬而未决。英伟达正受到国会、司法部、证券交易委员会及其自身董事会的调查。美国情报界似乎掌握了足以让黄仁勋陷入被动的情报；据报道，他有多次婚外情，包括与公司一名已婚女高管，以及与一名疑似中国间谍的女子。

记者们详细披露了他如何刻薄地对待员工，其中包括人身威胁和仪式化的羞辱。他定于下周二接受众议院多个委员会的闭门问询，并于两天后赴参议院作证。换作其他企业高管，这些丑闻中的任何一桩都足以断送职业生涯。对黄仁勋而言，这不过是一个寻常的周一早晨。

黄仁勋之所以不可撼动，源于他与特朗普总统的密切关系。2025年，黄仁勋和妻子洛丽到访马阿拉歌庄园，从那时起，他便开始经营这段关系。席间，他向特朗普讲述了自己如何从连锁餐厅Denny's的一名服务员成长为半导体企业首席执行官的动人故事。在为黄仁勋撰写传记的过程中，我多次听他讲过这个故事，始终百听不厌——尽管我确实注意到，每次讲述的细节略有不同。听得入迷的特朗普彻底被黄仁勋征服了。他也很喜欢洛丽，周一还称她是个“了不起的女人”，对丈夫“非常支持”。

到今年年初，特朗普和黄仁勋经常通电话。当国务卿兼国家安全顾问鲁比奥向他汇报了关于黄仁勋与黄乐的私情以及认为她是中国情报机构线人的细节时，特朗普不以为然。他反而邀请黄仁勋乘坐“空军一号”，随他一起会见中国国家主席习近平。《纽约时报》最终披露了这些情报调查结果，引发了一系列关于黄仁勋不当行为的爆料。12天前，英伟达董事会一致接受黄仁勋辞职。但在此期间，人工智能经济遭遇重挫，在特朗普力促黄仁勋复职后，董事会又一致投票同意让他回来。

特朗普采取行动并非没有理由：英伟达股价暴跌对全球经济构成了威胁。英伟达表现不佳时，整个股市都会受到拖累。相反，英伟达的成功会带动庞大的数据中心和开发商群体。黄仁勋就是英伟达，英伟达就是人工智能，而人工智能就是美国经济。我们的股市能否繁荣，在很大程度上竟取决于这一个人。

我理解董事会的考量。它不是道德警察，它的职责是推动英伟达股价上涨，而在这方面，没有人比黄仁勋做得更好。几名董事会成员本身就是凭借英伟达股票跻身亿万富翁行列的，其中一些人从公司创立之初就追随黄仁勋。再说，他们又能怎么办呢——对总统说不吗？

而且，不得不承认，黄仁勋的确是一位无可替代的商界人士。他一个人就能承担整个高管团队的工作。他是管理者、思考者，也是实干家。他是无情的运营专家、深谙客户关系之道的高手、善于发掘人才的伯乐，以及富有远见的战略家。他能提前数年预见新市场的出现，还能预测这些市场形成后的竞争格局。在报道蓬勃发展的人形机器人产业时，我发现，几乎每一台此类机器人的大脑都采用了英伟达的微芯片——因为早在这些机器人问世之前，黄仁勋就已指示英伟达着手打造这些大脑。

黄仁勋还有许多其他才能。他是一位出色的演说家——尽管他也会怯场。他风趣迷人，喜欢讲笑话。他的制图功底十分出色，能凭记忆画出一张精美的英伟达图形处理器分解图。他还能标出每个零部件，告诉你它的用途、成本，如果该部件未能按时交货，他会打电话痛骂哪一家台湾供应商。63岁的他依然精力充沛，运动能力出奇地好。如果英伟达董事会没有重新聘用他，他完全有能力创办一家与英伟达竞争的企业。

特朗普出面促成黄仁勋复职，也是在迎合普通股民。英伟达是散户投资者最青睐的股票之一，其知名度甚至超乎想象：今年早些时候，在北卡罗来纳州乡间打飞碟靶时，我向一位射击同伴提到自己写过一本关于英伟达的书。他立即在手机上打开自己的Robinhood账户，给我逐一介绍他买卖英伟达股票的记录；随后，他喊了一声“放靶”，半秒内就击中了两个目标。我发现，这类股东往往对英伟达究竟生产什么只有一个模糊的概念。但有一点他们很清楚：这只股票应该上涨。

然而，如果说特朗普促成黄仁勋复职有利于普通投资者，此举对法治而言则糟糕透顶。英伟达可能触犯了法律，必须受到彻底调查。2022年，拜登政府宣布限制英伟达最先进的芯片销往中国。作为回应，英伟达开始与东南亚的新合作伙伴开展业务。这些所谓的云服务合作伙伴在英伟达分配最先进的微芯片时享有优先待遇。鉴于2023年底英伟达的产品供不应求，这几乎等于给这些合作伙伴发了一张印钞许可证。这些合作伙伴大多位于新加坡，原本应将它们获得的搭载英伟达芯片的硬件设备安装到马来西亚的数据中心。然而，调查人员称，其中一些合作伙伴将设备转售给中国，绕过了出口禁令。

其中一家云服务合作伙伴的经营者韦兆伦积累的财富足以让他买下一栋价值4000万美元的豪宅。2025年2月，他被新加坡警方逮捕，被指将获配的英伟达芯片转售给中国。新加坡方面以洗钱和欺诈罪名对他提起指控，如果罪名成立，他可能面临最高20年的监禁。他表示不认罪。（英伟达表示在他被捕前已停止与他的业务往来。）

黄乐的公司也是英伟达的云服务合作伙伴，而她本人是黄仁勋的情人。2025年6月，新加坡警方对她进行了问询，并扣押了她的护照。警方于2026年2月归还了她的护照，后来表示美国司法部不予配合。她已被禁止入境新加坡，据报道目前身在中国。美国情报界认定她是中国情报机构的线人，她的公司则涉嫌将芯片转运至中国。（中国否认这一点。）

我想知道为什么英伟达将这两个人指定为优先客户。我想知道英伟达对这些及其他新加坡企业存有哪些疑虑，又采取了什么应对措施。我还想知道，在新加坡的销售额增至公司营收的22%之后，英伟达为何改变了会计核算方式。但我担心，我可能永远得不到完整答案。

美国商务部原本与新加坡警方共同展开调查，但在英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特直接给调查人员发送电子邮件，并特意提及他们的上司后，商务部被调离了此案的调查工作。司法部接手了调查——新加坡当局称，正是在这时，他们对黄乐的调查陷入停滞。特朗普对黄仁勋的支持向英伟达董事会释放出一个信号：联邦调查局不会查出任何对他过于不利的东西。我不禁怀疑，调查到底有多认真。

黄仁勋的复职也在职场女性能否受到公平对待的问题上释放了一个极其恶劣的信号。黄仁勋至少与两名下属有过婚外情：一名是已婚的医疗保健业务高管金伯莉·鲍威尔，另一名是路透社查明身份但未公开姓名的女性。周一，《华尔街日报》报道称，黄仁勋承认还有其他婚外情。

这些行为若发生在美国其他任何人身上都足以导致其被解雇，而他很可能几乎不用承担任何后果。事实上，他那些荒唐的情事甚至成了人们津津乐道的事情——周一，特朗普发布了一张网络恶搞图片，以自己遭遇暗杀未遂时那个著名的高喊“战斗！”的瞬间为蓝本，画面中黄仁勋满脸是血，挥舞着一件红色胸罩。这个玩笑表明，人们的行为准则正在倒退回《广告狂人》(Mad Men)所描绘的时代。这对女性来说意味着怎样一种更广泛的社会文化影响，想想就令人沮丧。

在黄仁勋传记《思考机器》（The Thinking Machine，中译《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》）的早期草稿中，我曾写道，他是历史伟人之一。后来我删掉了这句话，但现在我希望自己当初没有这样做。黄仁勋有多伟大，就有多可怕。

他是一位产业巨擘，从晶体管这一最基础的层面彻底重塑了计算机。但他也背叛了妻子、员工、公司，甚至可能背叛了自己的国家。他热情而富有魅力，爱开玩笑，举止谦和。但他同时也是一个自恋、自大、善于操纵他人的人——一旦脾气发作，他的表现就像一个心胸狭窄、缺乏安全感的暴君。

毫无疑问，他是一个复杂的人物。等到明年1月民主党人掌权，他们必将对他穷追猛打。但如果我是英伟达董事会的一员，面对该如何抉择的问题，我会选择谁同样毫无疑问。

欢迎回来，黄先生。我们还没来得及想念你呢。

Stephen Witt是黄仁勋传记《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》(The Thinking Machine)的作者。

翻译：纽约时报中文网

item.title: CIA 部分非机密信息泄漏
item.description: 中央情报局（CIA）和国家情报总监办公室（ODNI）最近发现了一起网络入侵事件，导致部分非机密信息遭到泄露。此次入侵影响了一个开源情报分析系统，机密信息未泄漏。开源情报旨在利用公开非机密信息搜寻情报线索，其涵盖范围广泛，包括可商业获取的数据集、社交媒体内容、卫星图像以及其它网络数据。开源情报结合其它数据源，经常能揭示出极具价值的情报。情报机构常将此类数据与其它情报来源综合使用以辅助分析判断。

item.title: 男性肥胖者服用 GLP-1 药物后改善了精子质量
item.description: 根据发表在《Biomedicines》期刊上的一项研究，男性肥胖者在服用 GLP-1 药物之后改善了精子质量和睾酮水平。研究针对了 108 名有肥胖症和/或 2 型糖尿病男性，服用 GLP-1 药物一年后他们的精子浓度显著增加。在服用 GLP-1 前样本中仅有略超 3% 的精子形状正常，12 个月的治疗后这一比例上升至 4.5%。具有前向运动能力的精子比例也从 23% 提高到了 38%。服用者平均睾酮水平上升 30%，雌二醇水平则有所下降。

item.title: 办好家门口的养老院
item.description:
2026-11-25 16:00:00

11月18—19日，全国老龄工作会议召开。会议提出，要把握老年群体的经济条件差异，注重服务保障的梯度供给；把握老年群体的养老方式差异，注重居家社区机构服务贯通协调；把握老年群体的城乡区域分布差异，注重政策的均衡性和精准性。

几天之后，11月23日，国家发展改革委、民政部等联合印发《“一老一小”服务体系建设实施方案》。针对养老问题，方案提出，到2030年社区养老服务机构和设施覆盖率达到70%，基本形成覆盖城乡、布局合理、价格可接受、质量有保障的普惠养老供给格局。 

社区养老，是在老人居住的社区内，通过嵌入式养老机构或上门服务等方式，为老人提供生活照料、康复护理等养老服务。2016年，国务院办公厅印发的《关于全面放开养老服务市场提升养老服务质量的若干意见》就提出，鼓励建设小型社区养老院，满足老年人就近养老需求，方便亲属照护探视。“十五五”规划纲要也明确，发展社区嵌入式养老服务，培育专业化、品牌化、连锁化社区养老服务机构。

在政策支持下，社会资本参与的小型嵌入式社区养老院在一些地方得到了发展，但也存在一些问题，为此，民政部、市场监管总局联合制定《养老机构基本规范》《养老机构重大事故隐患判定准则》等养老服务强制性国家标准，旨在保障养老服务安全，保护老年人的生命健康权益，将于2027年8月1日起实施。

这些强制性国标从发布到实施预留了1年时间，不过对于部分嵌入式养老院来说，满足要求需投入不菲成本进行改造升级。如根据规定，消防控制室要24小时双人值班，仅此项就至少需要6名持证的消防设施操作员，即便在二、三线城市，这也是一项不小的成本。国标也对养老护理员和老人的比例（护老比）提出要求，如完全失能和重度失能老年人，护老比不低于1∶5。要满足要求，养老院也需要雇佣更多人员。据《经济观察报》报道，有经营了10年左右的养老院，因盈利常年微薄难以承担改造成本，不得不关闭。

对养老机构进行规范，本意是通过规范管理，提高养老院的安全和服务水平，为老年人提供更高质量的养老服务。不过标准提高，养老院的成本不可避免要提高。如果不提高收费，养老机构可能难以盈利甚至陷入亏损，服务不可持续，供给会减少。如果提高收费标准，会导致更多老年人无力承担费用。

养老服务的质量、价格和可负担性是成反比的，质量越高，价格就会越高，可负担性就越低。这是无法避过的经济规律。破解之道，重在提供普惠养老供给，提高可负担性，政府可通过提供补贴等多种方式为养老机构更多支持，在管理上也要在规范和可负担性之间达到平衡。

正如全国老龄工作会议提出的，要把握老年群体的经济条件差异，注重服务保障的梯度供给。养老机构应该因地制宜，因人制宜。尤其是对于家门口的养老院，必要的安全和服务要保障，客观现实和普遍规律也需正视，最终尽可能留住、办好这些家门口的养老院，让老年人就近享受养老服务，颐养天年。

item.title: 走出漫长哀悼，她们在异乡重新看见母亲
item.description:
2026-11-25 17:09:30

十岁那年，中国女孩赌气说自己想去上吊，母亲在旁回了一句：“行，你去吧。”地球的另一端，一名从马里来到巴黎的女舞者，躺在产床上分娩，剧痛中惊觉童年时母亲带她经历过割礼，而远方的姨妈正催促她把同一把刀落在新生女儿身上。在伊朗首都德黑兰，在伊朗革命和两伊战争的炮火声里，一个年轻姑娘踩着邻居家的屋顶一路逃亡，几十年后，她在异乡照顾着彻底失忆、退行成孩童的母亲。

三个种族、三种层面的母女关系与女性记忆，被旅法戏剧人王婧写进了戏剧《我，她，她们》。2025年在法国首演并演出近二十场后，2026年10月，这部戏来到第十三届乌镇戏剧节。

100分钟的演出里，舞台上只有七把奶油白色的椅子。中国演员鲍烨露、拥有中国与安的列斯血统的法国舞者蒂舒·阿米纳塔·卡内（Tichou Aminata Kane）、法国演员爱丽丝·库德拉克（Alice Kudlak），在十五个碎片化的场景中交替扮演女儿与母亲，法语、中文、班巴拉语和波斯语在剧场里轮番响起。

戏在乌镇演了三场，剧场内外的反应分裂得颇具戏剧性。演出时，观众席里抽泣声几乎贯穿全程，散场后，一位三十岁出头的男观众在化妆间外等了四十多分钟，只为和主创聊上几句。有观众写来长信，向自己出生在福建闽南山区、一辈子不识字的母亲道歉。但在一场临时组织的观众交流会上，一名学编剧的年轻女孩当面抛出了尖锐的质疑：把伊朗革命和非洲女性割礼写进戏里，是不是在“投法国所好”“搞政治噱头”？

面对揣测，王婧感觉有点荒谬，她答：“这个作品中，对我来说最重要的就是真诚，没有一个故事是凭空发生的。”这部由她担任编剧、中国香港导演黄俊达担任形体设计，两人共同导演的作品，起点是她自己长达十余年未能走出的私人创痛。2008年，母亲突然离世，27岁的王婧离开中国，独自飞往当时一句法语都不会说的法国，住进一间12平米的屋子。在漫长的异乡生活中，她试图用一门陌生的语言处理与母亲之间未竟的告别，却在巴黎的地铁、排练场和日常相遇中，撞见了同样背负着家族伤口与迁徙记忆的异国女性。

排练初期，王婧在排练室里提起自己查到的数据，哪怕在巴黎北郊桑德利这样的现代欧洲街区，近年女孩遭受割礼的人数依然在上涨。全剧组人听完一度呆住。那些在新闻报道里显得遥远、宏大甚至带有猎奇色彩的词汇，忽然变成了每天擦肩而过的街坊日常。

王婧和黄俊达借由“等待”这一异乡人共通的身体处境，让东亚家庭隐秘的爱与窒息、部落习俗的身体烙印与战争年代的仓皇出逃，在同一个空间里彼此照见。

《我，她，她们》演出现场。受访者供图。

哪些要接住，哪些必须打破循环

2008年母亲离世后的很长一段时间里，王婧一动笔写这段记忆，就会卡在医院抢救那一幕。她试着写过几次，都没能写下去。直到2014年儿子出生，她自己成了母亲，法语里那个漫长的“deuil”（悼念期）才算慢慢过去，她得以退后一步，重新打量母亲的一生。2021年新冠疫情期间，她终于写出剧本的前三场，其中两场写的就是自己与母亲在中国的往事。写完这三场，她再次停笔，想把视野从私人哀悼里推开，写一写身边那些同样背负着家族记忆的女性。   

有一回在巴黎，王婧背着包带年幼的儿子下地铁台阶去看展览，一个十几岁的年轻人伸手偷走了她的钱包。王婧还没反应过来，身旁的儿子突然发出一声她从未听过的尖叫，浑身发抖，拳头攥紧，眼眶里全是泪。小偷被这声尖叫吓得腿软，扔下钱包跑了。自那以后，儿子每次进地铁都紧盯着前后左右，执意让母亲坐在靠里的位置。

看着孩子面对突发危险时的本能恐惧与无力，王婧忽然想起了母亲的青春期。她听母亲提过，虽然外公是参加过抗日战争的地下党员，但外婆是学校老师，动荡年代作为知识分子常年被拉出去批斗。王婧追问。仅仅被偷了钱包，尚且能在一个孩子心里留下长久的警觉，“看着妈妈被打，所有人辱骂她，你觉得一个青春期的孩子会不分裂吗？”。那一刻，王婧放下了对母亲严厉、多变脾气的多年困惑，绕开“原谅”或“不原谅”的评判，开始看见与理解。   

在戏里，演员鲍烨露饰演的正是以王婧为原型的中国姑娘。这种从私人脾性向时代印记的追溯，也是她进入剧本时的切口。鲍烨露比王婧小十二岁，在她看来，王婧母亲那一代人身上叠印着双重时代要求：社会要求她们“能顶半边天”、从内到外都要强悍，她们既没有现成的育儿参照，也从未接受过情感教育。“没有一个人想迫害自己的小孩，都是希望小孩好，但什么是好的方式，是社会给她的经验。”鲍烨露对南方周末记者说。   

当写作从中国家庭向外延伸，王婧把目光投向了在巴黎相遇的异国女性。在法国生活十余年，她常在欧洲主流媒体上看到扁平的标签，提起中国，便是“经济好、AI发达”或是某些固化的西方刻板印象；提起伊朗，也只剩几个政治概念。她不想重复这种宏大而空洞的叙事，选择把焦点落在“大时代变革下的小人物”身上，追问一个跨越国界的问题：在无数代际传递之间，什么东西你是要去传承的，什么东西是可以打破这个循环的？  

为了写好另外两种文化里的母女，王婧给自己划了一道虚构与纪实的边界。她创作的是虚构剧场，人物关系可以重组，但历史背景、地名、习俗不能凭空捏造。   

马里姑娘法蒂姆的原型，来自王婧在巴黎有轨电车上与一位中国编舞朋友的闲聊。朋友提起自己认识一位极有天赋的马里舞者，无证居留、孤儿，童年经历过割礼。王婧花了两周翻查档案，发现时至今日，马里24岁至49岁女性遭受割礼的比例仍在85%以上。她设法找到了原型本人，与对方聊了三十分钟。现实里的法蒂姆性格阳光，在餐馆洗盘子，生了几个孩子，早已不再跳舞。整场谈话里，她只在说起自己因拒绝给女儿做割礼而被整个家族视作耻辱、彻底断绝往来时落了泪。排练时，王婧还向祖籍马里的舞者讨教，把对方喜爱的马里女性舞蹈名称和居住的巴黎郊区地名写进了台词。

伊朗线的写作则始于一桩新闻：一名年轻伊朗女性因未佩戴头纱被警察带走后死在警局。王婧由此回溯到自己在巴黎第三大学读书时结识的伊朗同学，以及她们母亲那一辈的经历。她把关于1979年伊朗革命的厚重史料读了两遍，去听社会学家的讲座，采访了四位母亲辈的伊朗女性、三位同龄女性和三位伊朗男性。

在落笔后，她把剧本发给伊朗朋友逐一核对历史细节，避免陷入一厢情愿的文化误读。

《我，她，她们》演出现场。受访者供图。

撤掉法语这层保护壳

王婧二十七岁赴法后才开始学习法语，此前她一直用中文写剧本。创作《我，她，她们》时，她却提笔用法语写下全剧。这个选择乍看有些反常，但她在写作中摸到了其中门道。

王婧剖析，中文与自我贴得太近，一旦触碰家庭内部的隐痛，母语习惯性的迂回与羞耻感就会冒出来，写作者也容易下意识躲进修辞技巧里。法语对她而言是一门带有距离的语言，严格的动词变位像一把带鞘的刀，帮她切开那些在中文里难以直呼其名的记忆。她打了一个比方：“盛怒之下，我可以用法语说出无数的脏话，没关系，因为它对我来说就是过去了。母语说不出来，人是卡住的。” 

这种跨语境写作最终在舞台上留下了一种混合质地。法国观众常惊叹她的法语台词“像箭一样直接射出来”，不留情面，句子里却又带着中文特有的意象。例如她将皮肤上的淤青与女孩的名字“婧”叠在一起，译作“青色的女孩”，又或是写一根皮带既坚硬又残留着体温。

法语剧名Moi, Elles在发音上与单数Moi, Elle完全相同，在王婧的构思里，“她们”既指代母亲与女儿，也指代母语与故土。剧组没有用纯法语抹平差异，而是让法语和少量中文、班巴拉语、波斯语在舞台上交错。法国演员爱丽丝专门向一位伊朗长辈学习波斯语的语感，舞者蒂舒也向马里朋友逐句请教班巴拉语对白。

对鲍烨露而言，法语同样充当了保护壳。从2024年初剧本朗读起，她一直用法语排演这部戏。直到2026年8月，为了准备乌镇演出，王婧亲手将部分法语台词译回中文。语言的缓冲层一撤掉，排练场上的空气立刻变了。

鲍烨露回忆，9月排练医院那场戏时，她甚至没有刻意调动情绪，只是把中文台词顺了一遍。可排完那一刻，她和王婧谁都没法看对方的眼睛，两个人各自躲在排练室的角落里哭，哭完又笑出来，“觉得我们俩（像）神经病”。

在乌镇舞台上频繁切换中法双语，更让鲍烨露生出一种近乎“操偶师”的体感。她解释，说中文与说法语时，人的肢体反应与观众关系截然不同，“乌镇版演法是不一样的，因为它变成了服务于中文版的某些桥段转换的一种演法，戏和戏中间的逻辑改掉了”。

鲍烨露十岁起在国内接触表演训练，后来赴巴黎第八大学研习纪录剧场，既不走法国国立戏剧学院派讲究声腔韵律的路子，也避开了国内话剧学院的舞台腔。排练结尾读母亲遗信那段戏时，她刻意摘掉所有表演技巧，只要求自己把每一个中文句子平实、清楚地念出来。

语言带来的疏离与重塑，同样贯穿整个主创团队的跨文化协作。香港导演黄俊达早年在巴黎学习戏剧，近十余年频繁带团来内地巡演，北至哈尔滨。他坦言，用普通话受访或工作时仍会感到些许局促，远不如粤语来得贴切，但正是这种走出母语舒适区的适应过程，让人得以触碰不同地域的生活经验。

王婧也感叹，跳出中文环境后，她反而重新看清了汉字与传统戏曲的妙处，譬如西班牙导演在舞台上写下巨大的“怕”字，拆解出“心变成白色”的惊心动魄，也让她反观中国戏曲一桌二椅的写意传统。正如她在接受法语电台专访中所理解的那样，主动走入一门陌生的语言，并非背离来处，因为“迷失，正是为了重新找到自己”。

《我，她，她们》演出现场。受访者供图。

排练场里，“清理河道”

黄俊达早年毕业于香港演艺学院舞蹈学院，后在巴黎贾克·乐寇国际戏剧学校完成专业与师资课程。以往他的创作大多依靠肢体推进，这一次拿到王婧的本子却发现“文字量很大”。

排练初期，主创试过在台上放一把椅子、两把椅子，甚至把椅子高高吊在半空，最终只留下七把奶油白色的椅子。王婧避开了纯白与中国传统丧礼中的惨白，选了偏暖的奶油白色，她希望这些背负创伤的女性在台上保有从容的优雅，不至于一开口便坠入悲情。

黄俊达回忆，刚到法国求学时，自己曾在办理学生签证的机构里坐上一整天，法语尚不流利，既不知道还要等多久，也不确定自己是否排对了队伍。这种悬在半空的处境伴随着每一个异乡人，“等待”由此成了整部戏的动作定锚。

调度上，黄俊达刻意放慢节奏。前半段演员动作极简朴，像推开一扇门，把观众引进故事。到了后半段，即便台词触及战火逃亡或身体创伤，舞台上依然看不到大开大合的肢体。黄俊达解释，台词本身已有强烈的画面感时，过猛的动作反而挤占观众的想象，让语言和身体互相抵消。他看重“四两拨千斤”的分寸感，有时仅仅是生活里“很简单的坐下，很简单的看”，目光角度一变，空间就跟着变了。讲述伊朗革命逃亡的那场戏，台词里已经铺开巨大动荡，台上却只留下一个孤独的人坐在那里，一静一动之间，张力就出来了。

声音与灯光同样极度克制。法国音乐家乌列尔·巴特勒米读完剧本后告诉王婧，这些文字本身足够扎实，经不起任何装饰性表演，一旦配上一小段华丽音乐去“升华情感”，整出戏立刻会变假。因此，整出戏拿掉了所有写实音效，灯光也力求极简，只是2026年秋天在乌镇演出时，受限于场地、设备以及法国灯光设计师未能亲临现场，光影最终只呈现出五六成效果。

除了王婧与三位女演员，形体、作曲与灯光设计均由男性担纲。排练期间，三位男性创作者曾私下讨论，面对如此私密而残酷的女性创伤，介入的力道该停在哪里。王婧笑言，每当排练场情绪过于浓烈，黄俊达就像一位冷静的心理学家，用客观视角稳住节奏。鲍烨露也感慨，男女身处的社会位置不同，虽难达成绝对的感同身受，但剧组里的几位男性主创身上都带着难得的柔软，没有侵略性的说教姿态，让排练场保持着安全与信任。

三位女演员此前素未谋面，背景截然不同。演马里线的蒂舒是地下街舞与当代舞者，身体感知极为敏锐，却不习惯按部就班分析文本；演伊朗线的爱丽丝是典型的法国话剧演员，逻辑缜密、台词功底扎实，总爱逐字追问；演中国线的鲍烨露则习惯在观察与抽离之间寻找平衡。

剧本朗读进行到第二周时，排练室里的情绪一度决堤。三位演员在剖析角色时纷纷调动起各自隐秘的生命经验，迅速拉近了彼此距离。然而，随着创作深入，文化与工作习惯的差异很快浮出水面。法国演员热衷讨论文本，碰到中式表达总爱追问“为什么要这么写”，有时聊得太密，连一旁的男性主创都忍不住感叹“太多话了”。蒂舒习惯依赖即兴身体记忆，频频改动调度却不自知，直到王婧用手机录下视频当场回放她才察觉。

更深层的卡顿来自身份焦虑。爱丽丝反复叩问自己，作为一名与中东毫无渊源的法国白人女性，凭什么站在台上讲述伊朗女人的逃亡？鲍烨露则因角色直接取材于身旁的王婧，初期一度深陷私人情感漩涡，直到强迫自己退回演员的专业位置，将个人情绪与文本剥离。

面对三个截然不同的身体，黄俊达放弃了统一标准动作或繁复的心理分析，转而带着她们做纯身体层面的练习。三条故事线在舞台中段交汇时，他会播放音乐或现场拨响尤克里里，让三人先自由地即兴舞动，再由他剪掉多余动作。

在鲍烨露看来，王婧与黄俊达在排练场做得最多的，就是帮演员把多余的情绪擦干净。演员站在台上本就容易脆弱，触碰到私人经验时，常常下意识抓住不放，或者急着向台下证明“我感受到了”。排练时两位导演一直在提醒她们往回收，她把这形容为“清理河道”：“你把自己个人要处理的问题摘得干净一点，这条道路就像淤堵的河流一样，才能让河流流出来，而不是抓住它。”

《我，她，她们》演出现场。受访者供图。

一面照向各自生命的镜子

乌镇首演当晚，王婧在台下捏了一把汗，因为导演孟京辉也坐在席间。两人的戏剧路数截然不同，王婧自认与对方那种大破大立的风格相去甚远。散场后，孟京辉走过来告诉她戏很不错，还坦承自己前二十分钟睡着了，后来被现场音乐拽醒，越往后看越喜欢。

三场演出并非场场顺遂。第二场排在下午，对习惯欧洲作息的法国演员而言正值困倦的午后，剧场里观众进出频繁，手机接连掉在地上，加上场地闷热拥挤，整场演出的气口始终没能凝聚，鲍烨露下台后陷入了长久的自责。

王婧在排演过程中做过不少取舍。原剧本第十场写了一个十八岁的白血病女孩与婧在医院里的对话，篇幅原本是现在的两倍。排练到后期，王婧觉得这一场分量过重，容易消解尾声母亲离世的冲击力，便动手删去了一半。三位女演员极力反对，在排练室里哭着求她把戏加回来，王婧最终还是坚持了整体结构的平衡。

在巴黎演出结束后，不少法国观众在大厅里感慨舞台上的女性之间的姐妹情谊，认为演后交流构成了剧场与公众之间的对话，但也有人走出剧场时顺口发出地缘政治式的感叹，把中国故事套进了固有的西方认知框架。而在乌镇，一个五百人的戏剧观众群托人找到王婧，她便在河边抽出一个半小时与十多位观众席地而坐。那位学编剧的年轻女孩除了质疑题材，还批评全剧“没有情节高潮”，并建议王婧“下一次写一个让观众看得懂的作品，不要搞这么复杂”。王婧坦言，自己从不在动笔前揣摩观众想看什么，创作者的本分是提出问题，至于这面镜子能照出什么，全看观众各自的生命经验。

误读之外，陌生的生命也发生了意料之外的连接。在乌镇似水年华酒吧偶遇王婧时，主持人大佐掏出手机，给她看了两张自己走出剧场后连夜拼贴的电子明信片，画面上叠印着地图、战争影像与一行英文“Three women, one journey”（三个女人，一段旅程）。王婧觉得，“他总结得很好，他看到了命运的一种东西在里面”。 

首演结束，鲍烨露呼吸还未完全平复，在台上念出了年轻观众蘑菇写给母亲的信。信中说自己与母亲只相差二十二岁，却隔着九年义务教育、普通话普及与互联网浪潮，两人明明出生在同一个村庄，彼此之间却横亘着时代与语言鸿沟。今年年初，家里爆发了一次争吵，当蘑菇流着泪质问全家为什么只偏爱弟弟时，她第一次听见母亲说出埋在心底多年的恐惧：“老了你们都不会养我，我已经想好了，以后找个寺庙出家养老。”信的结尾说：“我一直看不见那个无法跟上时代、看懂世界的妈妈。抱歉，妈妈。”

鲍烨露观察到，当下亚洲女性观众对结构性处境的共情格外敏锐，但作为演员，她时刻警惕自己把别人的苦难变成舞台上的消费品。不排戏的时候，她常去打零工，做体力劳动，提醒自己永远是一个“幸存者”，不能站在高处俯视他人的生活。

乌镇演罢，《我，她，她们》陆续收到了来自澳大利亚、巴西、希腊以及非洲国家的艺术节邀约，黄俊达已经在琢磨，如果未来走进希腊的露天剧场，空间尺度又将如何重塑演员的身体。

戏演完了，台下常有观众跑来追问王婧同一个问题：戏里的伊朗母亲，最后到底有没有来到法国？王婧不肯把话说死，她觉得那位母亲或许已经死在战火与医院里，或许真的跨越边境见到了女儿，又或许只是女儿在异乡生出的一场幻觉。就像她在剧本里悄悄埋下的那些互文：伊朗母亲十岁出嫁，失忆后唯一记得的是十岁那年踮着脚往锅里倒热水的女儿；中国的婧在十岁那年与母亲爆发过最剧烈的冲突。不同国度的母亲表达笨拙关爱的方式，也都落在一顿热气腾腾的饭菜里。王婧未曾在戏里点破这些呼应，观众听见便听见了，没听见也无妨。

“作为写作的人，我把这些都藏在后面了。”她说。

item.title: Trump's intervention to get Jensen Huang reinstated was about more than Nvidia
item.description:
At the center of the White House's push to get Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia was a conviction that he plays a critical role in keeping the artificial intelligence sector competitive.

According to a source familiar with the matter, President Trump and Vice President Vance view Huang as a vital defender of open-source AI models — which offer users greater control, customization, privacy, and cost flexibility — and believe his leadership is necessary to prevent closed-source AI developers from consolidating power.

Trump and Vance worked through the weekend to bring Huang back. After behind-the-scenes persuasion from the White House, Nvidia's board staged a stunning reversal Monday, returning Huang to the CEO position.

Prior to the reinstatement, the president and vice president were briefed on the national security dimensions of the situation. Both concluded there was no evidence Huang had engaged in any illegal or improper conduct regarding US national security. According to the source, Trump believes maintaining a close working relationship with Huang offers the administration the strongest opportunity to safeguard national security and prevent advanced chips from reaching prohibited buyers.

Trump said during a CNBC interview Monday that Nvidia's board had sought assurances that Huang did not pose a national security threat due to his ties to Alice Huang, a Singapore-based Megaspeed executive suspected of links to Chinese intelligence with whom he had an affair.

Huang resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging that and other extramarital affairs, but was reinstated after just 12 days.

In a post on Truth Social on Monday, Trump urged the company to maintain strict oversight, writing, "NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security."

Trump also noted that his assessment aligned with the Justice Department's. A Justice Department official confirmed that Attorney General Todd Blanche spoke with the president over the weekend, and that the department has found no evidence of wrongdoing by either Huang or Nvidia.

Addressing reporters at a press conference Tuesday, Blanche said, "To the extent that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that's something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true," when asked whether Huang had been investigated.

Blanche neither confirmed nor denied investigations into any diversion of Nvidia chips to China, only noting that investigations are always happening and he can only say so much publicly.

Blanche called Nvidia a "good corporate citizen," noting that if it were subject to a criminal investigation or were obstructing the Justice Department, Trump would not have told the American public that the US government does not possess evidence that Huang engaged in any unlawful conduct.

"I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen directly to the board of directors," said Blanche.

Nvidia surged more than 30% on Monday, nearly reclaiming the losses following Huang's resignation. The stock skidded nearly 6% Tuesday to $155.38.

Nvidia stock fell more than 5% during premarket trading on Wednesday.

There are still myriad unanswered questions, including whether Nvidia's latest Blackwell chips were routed via Singapore's Megaspeed to China. Huang will face both closed-door and public sessions with lawmakers in Washington next week to discuss exactly what happened.

Follow Jennifer Schonberger on X @Jenniferisms and on Instagram.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo Finance at https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/why-trump-wanted-jensen-huang-back-at-the-helm-of-nvidia-224325153.html

item.title: 日本政府开发智能体打击盗版动漫
item.description: 日本文化厅正在测试一款 AI 智能体去自动识别和标记可能包含非法或盗版内容的动漫网站。测试结果显示其准确率极高。2025 财年针对国内的一项调查显示，AI 标记的 1168 条可疑 X 推文有 84% 是非法内容；AI 检测的 1564 个动画网站中 89% 含有盗版动画；1935 个漫画网站中盗版漫画比例高达 94%。2026 财年日本政府将监测范围扩大至海外。日本政府计划最早于 2027 年 3 月汇总并公布最新调查结果。

item.title: 6 people dead, including 2 children, after plane crashes off Mississippi coast
item.description:
Six people, including two children, were killed Tuesday when a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The Coast Guard said it had found the remains of all six individuals aboard a downed Cessna 210 aircraft approximately 2 miles northeast of Horn Island, Mississippi.

Officials said the plane descended at 10,000 feet per minute prior to the crash, NBC News reported.

Four adults and two boys, ages 8 and 10, were on board, Coast Guard spokesperson Juan Ros said.

Air traffic control in Mobile, Alabama, reported at about 3:45 p.m. CT that it had lost contact with the plane, officials said.

A search effort was launched by the Coast Guard and federal, state and local partner agencies.  Rescue efforts were called off after roughly four hours when officials located the remains of all six people within the fuselage of the aircraft.

"This is a heartbreaking outcome, and our deepest sympathies are with the families and loved ones who are facing an unimaginable loss," Cmdr. Trevor Blount, the Coast Guard sector mobile search and rescue mission coordinator, said.

"While this is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, we are grateful for the strong interagency coordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families." 

Horn Island is 12 miles long and the east end is around eight miles from Pascagoula, Mississippi. It is part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore.

The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) will investigate. 

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/6-dead-including-two-children-after-plane-crashes-off-mississippi-coast-073443244.html

item.title: 2 men charged after reported break-in at Prince William and Kate’s country home
item.description:
U.K. police have charged two men over a suspected break-in at Prince William and Kate's country home.

Two Albanian nationals, Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged with burglary and trespass after police were called to Anmer Hall, in Norfolk, England, on Monday night after reports of "suspicious activity" on the estate.

The family wasn't home, Norfolk police confirmed in a statement to Yahoo.

Prince William and Kate were instead thought to be at Forest Lodge, their main home near Windsor Castle, where they stay while their three children are at school in the local area.

Police said in a statement Tuesday, "Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary following an incident at a property on the Sandringham Estate last night (Monday 23 November). Police were called just before 6 p.m. following a report of suspicious activity at the address. Officers attended and specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the National Police Air Service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area.

"Two men were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass. They remain in police custody. The property was unoccupied at the time of the incident. Inquiries remain ongoing."

Kensington Palace said it would not comment on security matters.

Anmer Hall is Kate and William's country home, located on King Charles's private Sandringham Estate. It's a vast 10-bedroom property that was given to the couple as a wedding present from Queen Elizabeth II in 2011.

They used it as their primary home during the COVID-19 pandemic and now spend Christmas and other holidays there, enjoying privacy, peace and outdoor activities.

The family spends the majority of their time at Forest Lodge, which is about 20 miles west of central London and a 15-minute drive from Prince George's new $85,000-a-year boarding school, Eton College. His younger siblings, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, attend Lambrook, a coeducational private school an eight-minute drive from the house.

Forest Lodge is an ideal location for the family to be based, as William and Kate can easily reach the U.K. capital, where many of their public engagements take place. Today, William met with U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham at Burnham's London home and office, 10 Downing Street.

Kate, meanwhile, is awaiting the airing of her upcoming documentary, Heal. The "deeply personal" documentary covers Kate's diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer. It will be broadcast in the U.S. on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT on NBC, on Bravo at 11:30 p.m. ET/PT, and will be available to stream on Peacock from Dec. 1.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/article/2-men-arrested-after-suspected-break-in-at-prince-william-and-kates-country-home-134918079.html

item.title: NASA deliberately crashed into an asteroid. Now scientists are surveying the damage.
item.description:
A spacecraft has arrived at an asteroid to investigate the damage caused by an unprecedented cosmic crash.

In what may sound like the plot of a disaster movie, Nasa's Dart spacecraft deliberately smashed into the space rock in 2022 to knock it off course.

The Nasa craft was obliterated on impact. Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) mission, called Hera, is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision - with the first images set to be released later on Wednesday.

The asteroid poses no threat, instead this was the first ever test of our planetary defences to see what action we could take if a space rock was heading for our planet.

"Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact," said Patrick Michel, principal investigator of ESA's Hera mission.

The crash test focussed on a pair of asteroids: a larger one called Didymos - about 730m (2,400ft) wide - which is orbited by a smaller rock called Dimorphos, about 150m (490ft) wide.

The Dart spacecraft targeted Dimorphos, hurtling into the rock at 22,000km per hour (14,000mph). Images beamed back showed the asteroid's rocky surface coming ever closer until the feed cut out on impact.

It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 10,000km long (6,200 miles), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space.

The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid.

Before the collision it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the Dart crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes.

But the arrival of the second spacecraft, Hera, will help scientists to answer many more questions.

"Dart exploded in the asteroid, and therefore we don't have the information of what is its final state," explained Michel.

"The impact could have left a crater - and if it is the case, we need to understand the size and the depth. Or [the impact] may have entirely reshaped the asteroid."

The Hera mission will spend the next year studying Dimorphos, and take a look at Didymos too.

The spacecraft is packed with instruments, and it also has two small shoe-boxed sized satellites onboard, which can study the impact site up close, and then later land on the asteroid.

A key task is to measure the mass of Dimorphos, to work out how effective the spacecraft's shove was.

This information would be vital if we ever spotted a space rock that was on a collision course with Earth.

"It would help us to predict what would happen if we had to hit another asteroid," said Prof Simon Green, a planetary scientist who is on Hera's science team.

"We [could] measure its properties and say: 'Well, we need this mass of spacecraft, travelling at this speed, this early, in order to deflect it enough so that it misses the Earth'."

Asteroids pose a significant threat to our planet.

The biggest, which measure more than a kilometre across, could cause global devastation. But medium-sized asteroids around the same dimensions as Dimorphos could wipe out a city.

"We all know what happened to the dinosaurs, right? And we don't want that to happen to us," said Carolyn Ernst, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, who works on both the Dart and Hera missions.

"The good news for us is that there are far fewer potential threats out there in the Solar System than there were millions of years ago. But there are objects out there."

She said the biggest asteroids have been spotted, and none are heading to Earth.

"The smallest stuff isn't too much of a threat because our atmosphere protects us," she added.

"But there's a size range in the middle where we don't know where all of them are, and it could, if impacted, cause problems for humanity. And if we can find out about that and know about that, well, we sure as heck would want to try to stop that."

Scientists want to gather as much intelligence as they can about space rocks - to make us as well equipped as possible to deal with whatever the Universe throws at us.

A new mission is launching in 2027 to track potentially hazardous asteroids: a space telescope called the Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor.

There are also more visits planned to asteroids, including to one called Apophis, which is about 450m (1,480ft) long.

Apophis was discovered in 2004 and it was initially thought it might hit the Earth as early as 13 April 2029.

But now scientists understand its orbit better, and say it won't hit us for at least the next 100 years. Instead of a crash in 2029, it will fly just 32,000km (20,000 miles) above our surface.

This will give scientists the rare chance to study a space rock up-close.

Two spacecraft will head to Apophis, including Nasa's Osiris-Apex (which previously grabbed a sample from another asteroid called Bennu) and Ramses, a joint mission between ESA and the Japanese Space Agency (JAXA).

  • Spacecraft launches towards asteroid knocked off course by Nasa

item.title: Three states prepare for potential fallout from the Army's planned blast in Iowa
item.description:
The U.S. Army is planning to detonate 68 barrels of toxic lead-based explosives stored at a facility in Iowa Wednesday morning, despite concerns from environmental groups.

Officials insist a raft of safety measures is in place to limit a plume of lead particles that will drift from the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant after the detonation of the 5 tons of degraded lead azide. On Tuesday, the Army called for a 5-mile recommended evacuation zone to the southwest of the site "out of an abundance of caution."

Local residents within 20 miles also received an emergency notification to their cellphones Tuesday telling them to remain indoors with windows closed "to avoid airborne lead dust, noise and vibration."

At a press conference at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said there was a consensus among experts that "a controlled, mitigated detonation" of the entire U.S. stockpile of lead azide "is far preferable for public safety than an uncontrolled detonation."

"Inaction is no longer an option," added Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, the Army's leader of t

Sean Kaufman, of the Department of Health and Human Services, said Tuesday that pregnant women, children and those with chronic disease "definitely want to be out of that area."

The planned detonation is scheduled for Wednesday morning at 9 a.m. local time.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency is offering transportation and safe lodging for residents who are unable to evacuate on their own.

Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds backed the Army's decision on Thursday, writing on social media that she has asked for as much information as possible to prepare the surrounding area for the blast.

"I believe, based on the information I've been given, that the danger is immediate, and I trust the Army will do everything in its power to protect the people who could be affected," she wrote on X.

The announcement followed a judgment from the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Monday, which said the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency had "adequately incorporated safeguards to minimize the dispersal of lead dust."

The ruling acknowledged the detonation presented "real risks," but concluded that "we must acknowledge the realities of the situation: the degraded explosives present a risk of an uncontrolled and unplanned explosion, which would occur without the benefit of the safety measures that the Permit puts in place."

The court's decision came hours after President Trump announced that he had halted the plan. In a Truth Social post, Trump said that while he believes the "proper course is to get rid of this long-term problem," he would not allow the Army to destroy the material until federal courts sign off on the plan and Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand gives his approval. 

Sand, who takes office in January, has said the decision is up to the Trump administration "based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago."

The explosion threatens to send a plume of toxic lead dust over local communities, livestock and farmland in the surrounding area.

Environmentalists sued to stop the detonation last week, setting off a back-and-forth legal battle. The military has argued that the controlled detonation must take place soon, before impending cold weather potentially causes the material to combust on its own. 

Along with Iowa, Missouri and Illinois are also monitoring the situation.

Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe said in a post on X that the state's Emergency Operations Center was activated and that state agencies were "in constant contact" with federal partners. He added that impacts are expected to be "extremely limited" in the state.

Illinois Gov. Governor JB Pritzker said state agencies remained "on alert". "The detonation is expected to produce a dust plume containing lead particles that may travel beyond the installation and settle on surrounding surfaces," the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency warned in a statement on Tuesday.

Here's what led to the current situation, what the dangers are and what might happen next. 

How did we get here?

The roots of the controversy reportedly date back to at least March, when the Army discovered nearly 5 tons of deteriorating lead azide, a dangerous bomb-making material, stored at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa. According to legal filings, the lead azide had crystallized over the course of two decades, leaving it highly susceptible to exploding. The material is so volatile, the Army says, that the friction and motion of moving it somewhere safer would likely cause it to explode.  

According to the New York Times, the Army originally hired a chemical company to neutralize the material without an explosion, but later determined that detonating it was the right course of action. 

Earlier this month, the Environmental Protection Agency approved an emergency permit allowing the Army to carry out a controlled detonation of the lead azide.

The detonation was initially scheduled to take place on Friday. But local environmental groups filed a lawsuit aiming to stop the plan from going forward, arguing that the EPA failed to apply proper environmental standards when it approved the detonation, creating the risk of "immediate, irreparable harm" to surrounding communities. 

On Thursday, a federal appeals court issued an order temporarily blocking the Army from carrying out the detonation. But the Army argued in a filing Saturday that the situation has become so dangerous that it has the authority to proceed under a separate emergency exemption. 

The blast was on track to happen on Wednesday until Trump intervened. The court issued its ruling allowing the detonation to proceed about five hours after Trump's post was published. 

What are the risks?

Lead is a neurotoxin that poses a serious risk to those who are exposed to it, particularly pregnant women and young children. No one disputes that blowing up the barrels of lead azide could release dangerous material to the surrounding area. The Army shared modeling showing lead particles from the explosion traveling as far as 40 miles and airborne dust drifting up to 100 miles. 

The American Lung Association has advised people in the area to stay indoors for 24 to 48 hours after the blast to avoid exposure. 

The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services recommended residents take additional precautions, including turning off their home's air conditioning and heating systems, washing outdoor surfaces covered in visible dust with soap and water and washing hands before eating.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced Thursday that it has mobilized to assist the state in its monitoring and response after the detonation takes place.

The Army argues that, whatever risks the planned detonation poses, doing nothing creates the danger of something much worse. 

"The real choice … is not between a detonation and no detonation," the government wrote in a legal filing. "It is between a planned and mitigated detonation and an unplanned and unmitigated explosion."

But environmental groups have countered that the public was only given a few days' notice before the initial planned detonation, not nearly enough time for local residents to understand the full scope of the risk and take the steps they need to stay safe.

The groups also questioned how the Army allowed the situation to become so urgent when it had been aware of the material for at least eight months. Sand echoed that sentiment in a post on social media on Sunday.

"No good options exist and the situation is more dangerous and unpredictable than it ever should have been," he wrote on X. "Most clearly, since a contract to remove explosive risk was signed this spring, we must all be asking why it was cancelled, why nothing was done, and why we are rushing to demolition now in late November."

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/army-defends-plan-to-detonate-tons-of-lead-based-explosives-in-iowa-tomorrow-160114656.html

item.title: Kilmar Ábrego García arrives in Spain after flashpoint immigration dispute with U.S.
item.description:
Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported last year and sent to a notorious prison in his home country, left the U.S. for Spain on Tuesday, his team and the Department of Homeland Security confirmed.

Abrego Garcia arrived in Madrid early Wednesday morning, alongside his wife, an American citizen, and his lawyer, a representative for the family told CBS News. 

CBS News was first to report Abrego Garcia's plans earlier Tuesday.

Abrego Garcia, whose case became an early flashpoint in the debate over the Trump administration's deportation crackdown, was flying to Spain on a commercial flight Tuesday night, according to multiple U.S. officials familiar with the matter, who requested anonymity to talk about an arrangement that has not been disclosed publicly.

The exact nature of his arrangements and the conditions of his departure from the U.S. were not immediately clear. The federal judge in Maryland overseeing his civil legal case issued an order Friday that remains sealed.

In a statement, Abrego Garcia said he's leaving the U.S. "happy" and "with his freedom."

"In this case, despite everything they tried to say, every obstacle they put in my way, and every attempt to shame me, justice prevailed under this administration in a way that many people never thought was possible," Abrego Garcia said.

Abrego Garcia traveled out of the U.S. with his wife, Jennifer Vasquez, his attorney, Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg and representatives from We Are CASA, the U.S. advocacy group that has been helping him and his family.

Trump administration officials touted Abrego Garcia's departure.

"We are delighted to announce that Kilmar Abrego Garcia has self-deported from the United States to Spain," Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said. He reiterated the Trump administration's allegation that Abrego Garcia belongs to a gang — which his legal team has denied — and said he now "cannot terrorize innocent Americans."

In a social media post late Tuesday night, the Department of Homeland Security wrote: "To be clear: Kilmar Abrego Garcia departed the United States pursuant to a removal order. He paid for his own flight and received no incentives. He will NEVER be allowed back inside the United States."

The move by Abrego Garcia comes after the Trump administration spent months trying to deport the man, who came to the U.S. illegally 15 years ago and had been living in Maryland with his wife and children when he was detained by immigration authorities in March 2025. He was then deported to El Salvador and held for months in the country's CECOT prison, despite a previous court order barring him from being sent back to his home country. He was brought back to the United States last year to face criminal charges.

Abrego Garcia has maintained for more than a year that if he had to leave the U.S. again, he would be willing to go to Costa Rica, and designated the Central American nation as his preferred country of removal.

But the Trump administration had resisted that suggestion and instead unsuccessfully sought to deport Abrego Garcia to numerous African countries, including Uganda, Eswatini and Ghana. In more recent months, DHS said it was ready to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia — part of a broader practice of sending deportees to countries in Africa.

Abrego Garcia's departure from the U.S. came weeks after a hearing before U.S. District Judge Paula Xinis, who has been presiding over a civil case stemming from his deportation last year, was abruptly cancelled. The judge ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement last year to release Abrego Garcia from immigration custody and has continued to bar immigration authorities from detaining him while litigation continued.

But the Trump administration had sought to lift Xinis' orders, which it said were the only impediments to Abrego Garcia's "prompt removal." The Justice Department said in March that the government was "ready, willing, and able" to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia in West Africa.

Abrego Garcia's case gained national prominence last year after a top administration official acknowledged that his removal to El Salvador was an "error." Following his arrest by immigration authorities in March 2025, Abrego Garcia was among the more than 200 immigrants who were sent to El Salvador and detained at its notorious supermax prison, the Terrorism Confinement Center, or CECOT.

But Abrego Garcia had been granted a withholding of removal by an immigration judge in 2019, which prevented immigration authorities from deporting him to his home country of El Salvador because he was at risk of persecution by local gangs. 

In April 2025, Xinis ordered the Department of Homeland Security to bring Abrego Garcia back to the U.S., and the Supreme Court said the government had to facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody.

The Trump administration ultimately brought Abrego Garcia back to the U.S. in June 2025, but only after he was indicted on federal charges of human smuggling stemming from a 2022 traffic stop in Tennessee. Abrego Garcia pleaded not guilty and in May, a federal judge in Tennessee dismissed the criminal charges on the grounds that his prosecution was vindictive. 

The Justice Department has appealed that decision, and arguments before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit are scheduled for February.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kilmar-abrego-garcia-leaving-us-europe/

item.title: 车前子：把玩 | 走走看看
item.description:
2026-11-25 20:00:00

清代董诰《山水景致并书御制文津阁作歌扇》。故宫博物院藏。

为什么做扇子的竹子，要在冬天采？徐家东说过此中道理，只是我记不起了。一行有一行的门道。老药工曾经告诉我，枇杷止咳露药效不好的原因，在于现在采枇杷叶不讲究时辰。

好东西都有好个性。徐家东扇子，把把个性，一把是一把的个性，个性鲜明，七公里外分辨得出面目：这把扇子仿佛灯下苦读的文人，十年寒窗，长夜漫漫；那把扇子好像闺中少妇，腰身丰腴，掐得出纯净水。

也有肃穆如名臣，庄重似大将军，“呔！放马过来。”

一天下午，我观赏了徐家东这些年来制作的几十把扇子，有看一台戏之感。挑出两把，红男绿女，让它们演绎“情不知所起，一往而深，生者可以死，死可以生。”

他的扇子，内敛的，低语的，甚至缄默的，“是那处曾相见，相看俨然，早难道这好处相逢无一言？”

相看俨然，这是所有把玩的至上境界。

把玩是相看，或者说彼此守望，态度端正。

有时看徐家东扇子，看不懂之际，我就联想——徐家东扇子转化为古人法帖，比如这把扇子与《鸭头丸帖》挂钩，那把扇子和《韭花帖》搭讪，我就有点似懂非懂，直入微醺之境。

宕开来说，徐家东扇子像是写帖那路，二王书风，不是写碑之流，《爨宝子》《张黑女》，气韵确实生动，只是苏派扇子做出这风格，总要见外。扇子或许也有南派北派之分，“南派乃江左风流，疏放妍妙；北派则是中原古法，拘谨拙陋”，略抄阮元《南北书派论》，以作了断。需要加以说明的是，在中国艺术中，南派北派也好，南宗北宗也好，不是地理概念与划分，而是美学观念和归类。

雪中的徐家东，在竹林里采竹——选竹，像月下老似的，在选定的竹子上，系一红绳。

白雪。

翠竹。

红绳。

灰蒙蒙天气，徐家东下山喝酒，竹工伐竹的声音像露水滴入酒杯，举起酒杯，隔杯而望，远山一团和气的浓郁，“带几只冬笋炒雪菜呢。”

苏扇用竹采自安吉，也是几代人不断实践的结果。前几年有人不信，去宜兴采竹，做出来的扇子“啪啪”直响，好像过道里有个人拖着鞋皮走来走去，一，二，三，四，走过来走过去，没有根据地。

“带几只冬笋炒雪菜呢”，有鲜头的。所有味中，“鲜”最难说，“鲜”是道，味道味道，鲜味乃道。徐家东扇子的鲜头，也是难说，只能拿在手上，或许“则为你如花美眷，似水流年，是答儿闲寻遍”，“良辰美景奈何天，赏心乐事谁家院”，徐家东扇子，是昆曲，不是地方戏，更不是草台班子。当年徐慕云评价奚啸伯，言其“洞箫之美”；徐家东扇子，确有水磨调之美，或者昆曲里的笛子之美。

一把扇子亦如一把笛子，看谁吹奏，看谁把玩。

扇子是要上手的物事，用文字描摹十分困难，我只能多用比喻，有点乱了，乱了就乱了，乱世佳人，期待通感，“原来姹紫嫣红开遍，似这般都付与断井颓垣”，看到一把扇子——上乘之作——内心竟然有点苍凉：我说的是我，时间就这么过去了。

十年一扇。

十年一扇。徐家东做扇子，大骨不贴梁，因为所选之竹在五年以上。

采来五年以上的竹子，再存放五年。

手工不计，也要十年一扇。

徐家东告诉我：材料不好，就要贴梁，否则扇子夹不紧，像老化的松紧带那样松了。

松了，与所选竹子密度有关。这也就是徐家东自己要去安吉采竹的原因。

手拿一把雅致至极的扇子，如果碰巧看见堆放竹子的仓库，真有鸡窝里飞出凤凰之叹。手工，手工，其中要有多少手工？所以扇子定价，“物竞天择”，美也是要培养，要进化，“适者生存”，这里的“适者”，则是有缘人：一个人打开扇子，就像透过窗户，万物深邃，万物神秘，万物丰富，在扇骨那或幽或明的罅隙之中，活着，梦着，突然“啪”的一声，折叠起来。

扇子的地质学：如果褶皱的枢纽线与水平面有一定夹角，称此角为倾伏角，称这种褶皱为倾伏褶皱。

扇子的皱褶哲学：殊异点系列的多重部署，殊异点系列构成了皱褶，而折叠则是开创现时系列的潜在。

徐家东扇子是个“潜在”，在打开与折叠之间，扇子的手感，竹子的水线，一些材料纷至沓来，溢出故园池塘，春草青青，秋花赫赫。

草青花赫，活着，梦着，一把好扇子是活物，是梦游者，它脱离材料，又回到材料。

做折扇的材料比较丰富，吴门造扇，以竹为主。

竹之内：湘妃、梅箓（梅箓有多种写法，这里取其一，标记而已）、凤眼、玉竹、棕竹、芝麻竹、紫竹、罗汉竹……

竹之外：紫檀、海黄、檀香、乌木、老红木、鸡翅木、象牙、玳瑁……

好像无物不可造扇，只要扇起来有风，所以采竹就是采风吗？“瑶池阿母绮窗开，黄竹歌声动地哀。八骏日行三万里，穆王何事不重来。”看来黄竹还是做不了扇子。

宋代有位不出名的诗人，写有一首《扇子》诗：“蕲竹皮肤事业，齐纨手腕工夫。跳出二乘火宅，直饶一段冰壶。”

“手腕工夫”四字甚妙，制扇是手腕工夫，扇扇子也是手腕工夫。制扇手腕第一，现在先不说手腕工夫，说说材料——材质……

（“材料”与“材质”两字略有区别，材料是客观存在，材质是主观评判。）

手腕第一，材质也并列第一，两者不可或缺。

徐家东做扇子，手腕第一，材质也是第一，这在投机取巧、偷工减料的末法时代，实在难得。

一天下午，来位海上豪客，找到徐家东，定做二十把扇子，徐家东把他请到门外，说，笔直朝前，你走到大路右拐，不远，有家扇庄，批量生产。

徐家东告诉我，他根据材质决定扇式：半圆开花，金鱼头，大茄头，金钱白果，花瓶葫芦，大头古方，如意，宝瓶，金钱半圆，荸荠头，古排，小半圆，茄头，双茄头，燕尾，鱼尾，葫芦翻轮，全翻轮，小米头……

扇式要从材质中自然生长而出，不是硬做。“有些人不懂，拿来好材料，自作主张，要做这个半圆开花，要做那个小米头，他不懂，我懂，我就不做，不赚鸭孵卵铜钿。”

“鸭孵卵”，吴方言，指的是自以为是、不懂装懂、把事情搞砸的笨蛋。
